source_description: User-supplied local form-factor and ion-structure library audited before migration.

families.name: Gill

source_publication.title: Ion-ion dynamic structure factor of warm dense mixtures

families.notes: Figure 3 of Gill et al. (2015) explicitly identifies the state, methods, and reciprocal-space axis in inverse angstrom. The historical local filename contains QMD, but the source caption calls that curve TF-DFT-MD simulations of White et al.; the source wording is used in presentation. No additional coordinate scaling is applied to the imported CSV columns. No open numerical-data license was identified; the values are published by maintainer decision with license status NOASSERTION.

families.name: Jean2015
states: Al; rho=8.1 g/cc; Te=10 eV; Ti=2 eV

source_publication.title: Evidence for out-of-equilibrium states in warm dense matter probed by x-ray Thomson scattering

families.notes: The equilibrium and two-temperature curves are identified in Figure 1 of the cited paper. The local plot_jean.py leaves the reference k column unchanged, converts the project k grid with k_A^-1=k_Bohr^-1/0.529177249, and labels the common axis inverse angstrom.

families.name: wunsch2009
states: Be; rho=5.544 g/cc (3 rho0); Te=Ti=13 eV

source_publication.title: Ion structure in warm dense matter: Benchmarking solutions of hypernetted-chain equations by first-principle simulations

families.notes: The local plot_wunscher.py leaves every reference k column unchanged, converts the project k grid with k_A^-1=k_Bohr^-1/0.529177, and labels the common axis inverse angstrom. The real-space digitizations use the publication's angstrom axis.

families.name: starrett
states: H; rho=80 g/cc; Te=Ti=5 or 172 eV
W; rho=40 g/cc; Te=Ti=10 or 60 eV

source_publication.title: Electronic and ionic structures of warm and hot dense matter
source_publication.figure: The exact source panel for the local C 20 g/cc, 50 eV extraction is not yet independently verified.

families.notes: The core ion_structure_library retains C at 20 g/cc, 50 eV and the reference-only C pressure-ionization target at 3.7 g/cc, 8.62 eV. The dedicated starrett_single_species_2013_2014 package now contains the audited C 12.64 g/cc, Fe, H, and W files. Its panel-by-panel audit corrects two legacy assumptions: the PRE carbon and iron coordinates are r/R_WS rather than generic Bohr/angstrom coordinates, and the inherited Fe angstrom conversion was about 0.54 percent too large. It also distinguishes HEDP Fig. 1 SC-QM from Fig. 2 TF curves, records the PRE Fig. 5 erratum, and states that no W 60 eV SC-QM extraction exists locally. Three native Otter C/H states pass strict gates; rejected and uncalculated high-Z states remain explicit rather than reusing invalid legacy NPZ files. The exact panel for the separate C 20 g/cc, 50 eV extraction is still unresolved.

families.name: starrett2015
states: pure C rho=3.7 g/cc at 100 kK
families.notes: The nine CH1.36 states already live in the dedicated starrett_et_al_2014_mixtures_fig3 package; this inventory does not duplicate them.

families.name: argha
families.attribution: DFT-MD Sii(k) data provided by Dr. Argha Roy (private communication; unpublished).
families.notes: All six reference temperatures are retained in the dedicated argha_roy_carbon_sii package. The curves are labelled DFT-MD, matching the inherited plotting source and the maintainer's current identification; the intermediate Otter migration label DMF-MD is retained only in the dedicated provenance manifest. The reported uncertainty is not called one standard deviation because that interpretation has not been confirmed. The values are published by maintainer decision with attribution to Dr. Argha Roy and license status NOASSERTION. The displayed 20, 30, 40, 50, and 100 eV curves are current Otter calculations that pass strict electronic, threshold-state, HNC fixed-point, and transform-closure gates; the 1 eV reference file is retained but not displayed.

families.name: max2022

candidate_publication.authors: M. Schörner, H. R. Rüter, M. French, and R. Redmer
candidate_publication.title: Extending ab initio simulations for the ion-ion structure factor of warm dense aluminum to the hydrodynamic limit using neural network potentials

families.notes: The two states occur in Figure 2, whose black curves are 32000-ion NN-MD and red symbols are 125-ion DFT-MD; the published curves are vertically offset, whereas the local CSV values have already had the offsets removed and tend to one. The legacy notebook labels both files DFT-MD, but that attribution is demonstrably unsafe for the 8.1 g/cc, 5 eV file: a 125-ion cell at that density has L approximately 8.843 angstrom and therefore k_min approximately 0.711 angstrom^-1, while the CSV contains points at 0.235 and 0.508 angstrom^-1 that occur only on the NN-MD curve. At 4.712 g/cc, 1 eV the plotted NN-MD and DFT-MD traces overlap too closely to identify the extraction without its missing digitization metadata. No open numerical-data repository or redistribution license was found. The family is therefore inventoried but not promoted to an Otter benchmark until the authors provide curve-resolved tables and a usable permission or license. Legacy Otter/PAMD NPZ filenames also disagree with embedded temperatures and are not accepted.

families.name: Zak_2025
states: Al; rho=2.7 g/cc; Ti=1 eV; Te=1,10,30 eV

source_units.r: bohr (the publication labels the axis r [au])

source_publication.authors: Z. A. Johnson, N. R. Shaffer, and M. S. Murillo
source_publication.title: Quantum Ornstein-Zernike theory for two-temperature two-component plasmas

families.notes: The dedicated Johnson benchmark retains the locally available Te=1,10,30 eV curves; the paper's Te=3 eV panel is not present in the source library. Direct inspection of Figure 2 shows r [au], so the coordinates are Bohr. The legacy plot_zak.py axis label r [angstrom] is a unit-label bug and is not propagated. The paper states that numerical data are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request; provenance as author-provided versus locally digitized remains unresolved. The values are published by maintainer decision with article and panel attribution and license status NOASSERTION.

families.name: non_equlibrum
states: C; rho=3.51538 g/cc; several Te/Ti combinations
families.notes: Contains only old project NPZ outputs and no independent reference curves; useful for two-temperature regression, not a literature benchmark.

families.name: max_C
families.notes: The 50 eV carbon data duplicate the argha family. The 300 K file has very large crystalline/solid-like peaks and lies outside the homogeneous atomic-fluid PA-HNC validation scope.

reasons: Several filenames disagree with their embedded thermodynamic metadata.
At least one W 60 eV archive contains grossly nonphysical values.
An accepted result must be regenerated by Otter and load with allow_pickle=False.
